title: Pre-Analysis — Boost Pump Inlet Housing Compliance Extension to the Remaining Fleet
abstract: Closed pre-analysis of a proposed revision extending the airworthiness directive compliance route for the inner tank boost pump inlet housing to the aircraft still outside the current effectivity block.

sections.objective: Establish what has to change in the published data if the inlet housing replacement is to serve as the compliance route for the remaining aircraft, and confirm that the bonding evidence the directive closure depends on is actually generated by the published installation task rather than assumed. The order was raised by the fuel systems office after the authority asked how compliance is demonstrated on aircraft that took the housing outside the retrofit bulletin, during the last surveillance visit.
sections.findings_summary: Four items were confirmed and one of them had to be closed before the answer could be given to the authority. The retrofit bulletin carries the compliance statement, and its effectivity block stops short of the aircraft in question, so an aircraft outside the block has the hardware but no documented compliance route. The installation task does generate the bonding evidence, but it records it as a workshop measurement rather than as a released record, which is not what the closure argument assumes. The fault isolation procedure and the illustrated parts list both need the housing standard shown per aircraft rather than per part number, because the fleet now carries both and the pump is interchangeable while the housing is not.
sections.next_steps: The extension was cleared to proceed on condition that the bulletin effectivity is amended before the next surveillance visit and that the installation task is reissued with the bonding measurement recorded as a released value. The fuel systems office was asked to write the compliance argument once, in the bulletin, and to have the parts list and the fault isolation procedure reference it rather than restate it, which is how the two drifted apart in the first place.

similarity_seeds: compliance route for a fuel pump housing directive

tasks.title: Trace the compliance statement through the published data
Search fuel distribution data referencing the housing and the pump
Confirm how the bonding evidence is recorded in service
Check the fleet position against the current effectivity block

expected_findings.rationale: The compliance statement lives in the bulletin and its effectivity block stops short of the aircraft in question. Those aircraft carry the correct hardware and have no documented compliance route, which is exactly the question the authority asked.
expected_findings.resolution: Amend the bulletin effectivity to cover the remaining aircraft before the next surveillance visit, and state the compliance argument once in the bulletin only.

expected_findings.rationale: The installation task does generate the bonding measurement the closure argument depends on, but it records it as a workshop value in the job card rather than as a released record against the aircraft. The evidence therefore exists and cannot be retrieved, which is the worst of both positions.
expected_findings.resolution: Reissue the task with the bonding measurement recorded as a released value against the aircraft, with the acceptance limit restated.

expected_findings.rationale: The low pressure with normal quantity procedure identifies the installation by pump part number. The pump is interchangeable between the two housing standards and the housing is not, so the procedure cannot tell the mechanic which inlet geometry is fitted and sends half the fleet to the wrong acceptance figure.
expected_findings.resolution: Key the procedure on the aircraft housing standard rather than on the pump part number, and add the standard to the preliminaries.

evidence.similarity_note: Both name the inlet housing, the pump and the seal set in the same terms and reference the same installation drawing.

expected_findings.rationale: The figure lists the two housings as alternates without saying that the choice is fixed by the aircraft rather than by the mechanic. Ordering against the figure alone produces the wrong housing about as often as the right one.
expected_findings.resolution: Replace the alternate pair with two effectivity keyed items and add a note that the housing is not interchangeable.

expected_non_findings.reason: Shares a wing zone with the subject and is retrieved on any zone search of the wing box area. It repairs a fixed trailing edge panel at a fairing attachment land, well outboard of the inner tank, and has no connection to fuel distribution.

type_data.conclusion: Issued 2026-05-19. The compliance gap is documented and closable by an effectivity amendment plus a change in how the bonding measurement is recorded.
